senses.gloss: vaḍa (m., = AMg. id., Skt. and Pali vaṭa), banyan: Kv 〔8.3〕, in a list of flowers, -mahāmāndāra-vaḍāudumbarapuṣpa-.

vaḍḍa, adj. (cf. next; Deśīn. 〔7.29〕 = mahān, comm.; Hem. 〔4.364〕; AMg. vaḍḍa-kumārī, old maid, supporting Senartʼs derivation, 〔ii n. 541〕, from Skt. vṛddha; see Edgerton, JAOS 〔69.229〕, largely anticipated, as I learned too late, by Lüders, KZ 〔52.106—9〕), large, big, fat; of birds in captivity, fattened for slaughter and sale as food: vaḍḍa-vaḍḍā(ni) Mv 〔ii.241.15, 17, 20〕; 〔242.7〕; vaḍḍo (so read with mss., if not vaḍḍī-, see next) bhaviṣyati 〔242.14〕; of udumbara fruit, vaḍḍa-vaḍḍāni 〔246.11〕; in 〔249.19〕 (vs) mss. vaḍḍā ca vṛndi, (your) body (see vṛndi) is big.
Vaḍi, n. of a yakṣa: Māy 〔236.28〕.
Vaḍika, n. of a rich householderʼs son (hero of Av ch. 6): Av 〔i.28.3, 13〕 etc.
vaḍḍī-bhavati (see prec.), gets big, fat, of birds, as under prec.: Mv 〔ii.242.2, 4〕, and in 11 read vaḍḍībhūto; in 14 perh. vaḍḍī-(mss. vaḍḍo)-bhaviṣyati.
[vāḍaka, nt., mss. at Mv 〔i.340.12〕, should = Skt. vāṭaka (pw) = vāṭa, enclosure; but Senart is prob. right in emending (to chātrakaṃ, or perhaps better) to chattrakaṃ, q.v.]

? vāḍita, ppp. (to Skt. Gr. vālayati, beside Skt. valayati, causes to roll), prob. intended in Divy 〔505.10〕 (sā) naus taiḥ (sc. sūkaraiḥ) parispandamānair vāḍitā (for vālitā), was made to roll (ed. bāḍitā, said by Index to mean sunk; mss. voḍitā, voditā, vāditā).
vāḍiśika, m. (= Pali bālisika, Skt. baḍiśa, vaḍ˚, [] plus -ika), fisherman: ˚kena … sāmiṣaṃ vaḍiśaṃ prakṣiptaṃ Śikṣ 〔94.15〕.
